title: Local Density Approximation and Other Limit Regimes for a Homogeneous Bose Gas with Repulsive Three-Body Interactions in Low-Dimensional Space
authors: Thi Anh Thu Doan, Dinh-Thi Nguyen
abstract: In the whole space of low spatial dimensions, namely $d \leq 2$, we study the minimizers of an energy functional with an attractive cubic nonlinearity and a repulsive quintic nonlinearity, which describes a quantum Bose gas with a two-body attraction and a three-body repulsion. We prove the existence of minimizers at fixed effective statistics parameter. In the limit of a large effective statistics parameter of the mass-critical nonlinearity (with respect to the kinetic energy), we derive an effective Thomas-Fermi-like model for the homogeneous Bose gas. We also consider other limit regimes depending on the mass-critical nonlinearity.
summary: This paper rigorously studies the ground state of a Bose gas with competing two-body attraction and three-body repulsion in low dimensions. By analyzing the energy functional in various limiting regimes, the authors derive an effective Thomas-Fermi-like model. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding the physics of interacting quantum gases where higher-order interactions are crucial.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the ground state properties of a homogeneous Bose gas characterized by competing attractive two-body and repulsive three-body interactions in low spatial dimensions ($d \le 2$).
main_result: The authors rigorously derive the existence of minimizers and establish the convergence of the system's energy functional to an effective Thomas-Fermi-like model in specific limiting regimes.
method: The analysis employs variational principles, scaling arguments, and advanced convergence theorems (like Fatou's lemma) to rigorously derive effective nonlinear Schrödinger equations from the original many-body Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous Bose gas whose energy is modeled by a cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) functional, incorporating terms for two-body attraction and three-body repulsion.
key_observables: The primary observable is the ground state energy, and the derived density profiles ($ho_{TF}$, $u_0$) are key diagnostics.
important_parameters: Dimensionality ($d \le 2$), the coefficients governing two-body attraction ($a$), and three-body repulsion ($b$), as well as various limiting parameters ($a_0, b_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to homogeneous systems, and the Thomas-Fermi approximation relies on neglecting the kinetic energy term in the large effective statistics limit.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the existence of minimizers for the NLS functional. It then systematically analyzes different limit regimes (Thomas-Fermi, 1D, 2D) by showing the strong convergence of the sequence of minimizers to the corresponding limiting profile, proving the effective model's validity.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding how higher-order interactions (three-body) stabilize quantum gases in low dimensions, leading to the derivation of simplified, yet physically accurate, effective models like the Thomas-Fermi approximation.
